scope: Exclusive source semantics of original #2029 daemon startup status after main #2026; host startup/custody/retained state, status request admission/response, shared getter and IPC feature consistency. Fourteen pinned files including nine narrow ownership/module/cfg dependencies. No gate/predicate/queue/test/whole-PR review.

semantic_contract.claim: Status and ordinary recovery admission use the same two HostState signals. Explicit retained failure outranks outstanding custody; otherwise nonempty custody is Restoring and only empty custody with no retained failure is Ready.
semantic_contract.limit: Ready reports this daemon startup-recovery admission state, not all conversations recovered and not an atomic promise that later shutdown/request state cannot change.

semantic_contract.claim: Retained recovery is sticky. Only construction initializes None; retain_startup_recovery sets the first error and preserves it. Exact-worker completed Close removes custody without clearing the retained error. Ordinary-exit ownership is preserved when the late failure arrives.
semantic_contract.limit: No runtime Close/reaper claim; underlying cleanup proof remains inherited.

semantic_contract.claim: Initial empty flags are not externally served while synchronous boot restore runs. Binding precedes restore, but listener acceptance/handlers follow restore. A failed restore with live terminal/chat owners retains recovery; a failure without owners aborts instead of serving empty Ready. Recovery-only boot omits autonomous producers.
semantic_contract.limit: Restoring is not established as a streamed progress response during the synchronous boot body. An already queued socket connect is not a completed status handshake.

semantic_contract.claim: Existing terminal adoption publishes exact parent ownership and inserts startup custody under one HostState lock before the worker may CommitAdoption. Success retains custody through descriptor publication; retained errors set sticky recovery, and changed parent/pane/publication fails preserve recovery rather than returning Ready.
semantic_contract.limit: TerminalStartError alternative outcome proof and worker native behavior were not re-audited.

semantic_contract.claim: Main #2026 supplies exclusive ChatRestore classification. Retained wins over Codex-listener classification, then nonretained managed Codex listeners, then relaunch. Each loop takes only its category; the final relaunch loop excludes retained actors, so the new status API does not restore an already reattached actor again.
semantic_contract.limit: The category fix is already main #2026, not a new #2029 finding.

semantic_contract.claim: A retained-native refusal is intentionally per-conversation. It records exact adoption failure and unattached evidence, blocks paired replay for that refused source, writes recovered/unattached evidence before checkpoint consumption, and passes the refused IDs to the subsequent orphan pass so they are not immediately retried. Such a refusal can coexist with daemon Ready; it is not global Retained startup custody.
semantic_contract.limit: Whether a particular saved presentation must fail window readiness is the separate gate/recovery-collector review, not this API status.

semantic_contract.claim: Native reattachment remains the inherited no-launch path. It authenticates the holder and exact issued descriptor/pair, enrolls pending authority before installation, commits helper installation before publishing the new source, records authenticated registry ownership, revalidates daemon/pair/transition identity, then exposes the exact record. The new getter neither mutates nor clears these durable pending/committed owners.
semantic_contract.limit: These helpers are byte-equal to main4429 and were traced only for this status join. No full provider/rollback/launch ownership certification.

semantic_contract.claim: StartupState inspection passes both recovery admission checks and is classified read-only for authenticated agents. It returns a snapshot under HostState with no events/effects. The normal wire requires matched protocol128 and current complete daemon proof before this handler.
semantic_contract.limit: Committed ordinary shutdown/upgrade can still refuse the request through existing admission; that is an error, not a fabricated Ready.

semantic_contract.claim: ControlClient::startup_state uses the existing connected client's strict request path. It neither discovers a socket nor autostarts a daemon nor selects/falls back between local and remote. The request carries the pinned proof and the reply validates version, full proof and request ID.
semantic_contract.limit: Full caller endpoint selection and UI gate behavior are separate ownership. Real selected-remote/native evidence remains missing.

semantic_contract.claim: Shared IPC request/response/status type and ControlClient are available in CLI/HOST/UI source graphs; host-only state references remain host gated. The request and response append to their enums and both sides reference the one common protocol128 constant.
semantic_contract.limit: Source/API consistency only; no compiler or protocol-runtime claim and no protocol allocation decision made.
